cryptohome: Expose mount operations in a single function. In order to move cryptohome mount operations out of process, first we need to expose them as a single function in the helper. The reason for this is pretty straightforward: when executing out of process, the helper needs to be able to carry out all the mount operations in a single invocation. The easiest way to ensure that this will be possible is to perform all mount operations as a result of a single function invocation. Then we change the function invocation to a helper executable invocation and we're done. This continues the work in the previous CL by transferring enough state to the MountHelper class to allow regular user mounts to be completed with a single call to the helper. In order to make the helper API less overly verbose, this CL also introduces an Options struct for the helper. As opposed to ephemeral mounts, where the entire *Inner function could be moved to the helper, for regular mounts the *Inner function does quite a bit of key manipulation. Per the design these should stay in cryptohome and not be done in the helper, so for regular mounts the helper calls happen inside of the *Inner function instead of fully replacing it. This is not a big deal since seam between the Mount class and the helper is still pretty obvious since key operations happen first and mount operations happen later. The next CL in the series will move unmount calls to the helper, in preparation for running things out of process (this is the plan at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hSUSuIQLZvH1OVwn7N8lDIT7lFUEeHkmFDXQduBccho/edit#.) This CL is a net addition of fewer than 100 lines. Most of it is code moved around. BUG=chromium:985492 TEST=Unit tests pass. TEST=Add new user to Chromebook successfully. TEST=Log in, create local data, log out. TEST=Log back in, local data is still present.
